findings.claim: The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a real CSS property in any IE/Edge version. IE10/11 use `-ms-flex-align`, which the mixin already emits on line 120, so the `-ms-align-items` line is dead output.

verifier.reason: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:117-123 defines @mixin align-items emitting -ms-flex-align on line 120, -ms-align-items on line 121, and standard align-items on line 122. No version of IE or Edge ever supported -ms-align-items (IE10/11 use -ms-flex-align and IE11/Edge support unprefixed align-items), making line 121 dead CSS output.

findings.claim: The order mixin passes `$val` directly to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group`. Those legacy properties are 1-based, while `order` is 0-based, so ordering in older WebKit/Firefox is off by one, and a value of 0 is invalid.

verifier.reason: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:125-131, `@mixin order($val)` passes `$val` directly to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` (line 126) and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` (line 127) without adding 1. Because those legacy 2009 flexbox properties are 1-based (default 1, positive integers per spec/WebKit) while `order` is 0-based (default 0), values are off by one relative to unstyled siblings and `0` is invalid in legacy WebKit.
